newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Prairie wheat average-good despite fusarium.
newsitem.headline: Canada Prairie wheat average-good despite fusarium.

text.p: Canada's Prairies wheat and durum crops were rated average to good despite downgrading factors such as fusarium headblight, ergot and wheat midge, crop experts said.
"Overall, the condition of the wheat harvest is average to good," Canadian Grain Commission chief grain inspector Len Seguin told Reuters.
Grain standards are set in November by a farmer and industry committee based on 25,000 samples tested by the CGC.
Fusarium concentrations ranging from 0.01 of a percent and up were found in 36 percent of Manitoba's wheat, he said.
"While it's there in a wide number of samples, there is a grading system in place to make sure that it's not present in the high quality grades," Seguin said.
Fusarium in varying degrees was detected in 26 percent of Manitoba's durum wheat crop.
Fusarium (scab) struck Manitoba's Red River Valley and was present in some wheat northwest to Dauphin and into bordering crop districts of eastern Saskatchewan in July.
The fungus is brought on by prolonged rain during the heading stage and can produce vomitoxin which, in high levels, can cause nausea.
"There's insignificant (fusarium) levels in Saskatchewan and none at all in Alberta at this point," Seguin said.
Ergot, a fungus that strikes cereals in the flowering stage, was found in samples from the eastern Prairies.

Some 2.5 percent of hard red spring wheat in Manitoba showed signs of ergot damage in varying degrees, as did 11.6 percent in Canada Western Extra Strong, a variety of hard red spring used in frozen dough, Seguin said.
Only 0.5 percent of Saskatchewan's hard red spring wheat showed signs of ergot damage, while six percent of CWES samples were damaged. No damage was found in Alberta samples.
Wheat midge insect outbreaks are usually localized and of short duration but can damage quality.

"Midge damage is not terribly significant but it's most pronounced in Manitoba and Saskatchewan affecting about three to four percent of the durum, red spring and Extra Strong, and we haven't seen it at all in Alberta," Seguin said.
